statements.status_notes: GHSA-r7wm-3cxj-wff9 is a memory-exhaustion flaw in jackson-core's non-blocking parser when an integer token spans input chunks and maxNumberLength validation is not applied. The staged 1.6.0.1 image uses fixed jackson-core 2.21.5 on the application classpath; Scout identifies the affected 2.21.2 and 3.1.2 PURLs only inside hazelcast-5.7.0.jar. Bytecode scans found no DataHub application class or non-Jackson Hazelcast class referencing either relocated async-parser package or the createNonBlockingByteArrayParser, createNonBlockingParser, or NonBlockingJsonParser symbols. The vulnerable shaded code therefore has no execution path in this image.

GHSA-r7wm-3cxj-wff9 is a memory-exhaustion flaw in jackson-core's non-blocking parser when an integer token spans input chunks and maxNumberLength validation is not applied. The staged 1.6.0.1 image uses fixed jackson-core 2.21.5 on the application classpath; Scout identifies the affected 2.21.2 and 3.1.2 PURLs only inside hazelcast-5.7.0.jar. Bytecode scans found no DataHub application class or non-Jackson Hazelcast class referencing either relocated async-parser package or the createNonBlockingByteArrayParser, createNonBlockingParser, or NonBlockingJsonParser symbols. The vulnerable shaded code therefore has no execution path in this image.

The built image SBOM locates jackson-core 2.21.2 and 3.1.2 inside hazelcast-5.7.0.jar in nifi-hazelcast-services-nar, and jackson-core 2.21.3 inside parquet-jackson-1.17.1.jar in nifi-iceberg-parquet-writer-nar. NiFi's Maven dependency management cannot directly replace these embedded copies. Remediation requires upgrading the enclosing artifacts: Parquet 1.18.0 embeds jackson-core 2.22.1 but requires compatibility validation, while Hazelcast currently has no newer release that embeds fixed jackson-core 2.x and 3.x versions.

These jackson-core copies are shaded inside upstream fat-jars bundled by Druid's deltalake/orc/parquet extensions (hadoop-client-runtime and parquet-jackson), not Druid's own managed jackson. Standalone jackson-core copies in the Spring Boot fat jar are forced to 2.21.4 and tools.jackson 3.1.4 during the image build. Remaining findings are shaded inside hazelcast-5.7.0.jar (2.21.2 / tools.jackson 3.1.2) or parquet-jackson-1.17.1.jar (2.21.3). Those classes are unreachable by Gradle resolutionStrategy; Hazelcast 5.7.0 is the latest 5.x release and parquet-jackson 1.17.1 is the latest bundle embedding jackson 2.21.x.

The jackson-core instances used by neo4j have been bumped to a fixed version. The remaining jackson-core is shaded and relocated inside parquet-jackson JARs, which no fixed parquet release replaces. The vulnerable code is the non-blocking async parser, which accumulates integer digits across chunked feeds without enforcing the number-length constraint. The parquet libraries never create a non-blocking parser, so the vulnerable path is not reachable.

jackson-core 2.18.6 is bundled inside ray_dist.jar, which ships with the Ray Python package. The vulnerable path is the non-blocking async parser, which accumulates integer digits across chunked feeds without enforcing the number-length constraint, and is reachable only through Ray's Java runtime. This image ships no Java runtime, so Ray never starts a Java worker and the bundled classes are never loaded.

jackson-core 2.21.3 is shaded inside parquet-hadoop-bundle 1.17.1 (latest on Maven Central). DHI forces that bundle over upstream 1.17.0, but no published parquet-hadoop-bundle yet embeds the 2.21.4 fix for GHSA-r7wm-3cxj-wff9. The vulnerability affects async JSON parsing with unbounded number length, but Elasticsearch's typical deployment behind reverse proxies with request size limits provides some mitigation.
